slides.text:
**How Strata runs a 125-billion-parameter model on one gaming GPU.**

Developers are split on whether this is a real trick or just hype.

Either way, the technique behind it is worth understanding.

panel.small: params squeezed onto a single 24GB GPU

slides.text:
**Strata is a runtime built by developer Niko1221 to run huge models on small GPUs.**

It only loads the slice of the model a given token actually needs.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next is a mixture-of-experts model with 24,576 tiny expert networks.

Each token only activates a handful of those experts.
bullets: 24,576 experts make up the full model.
Only a few experts fire per token.
Most of the model sits idle for any given word.

slides.text:
Strata keeps the busiest experts sitting on the GPU itself.

Everything else waits in system RAM, or further out on disk.
bullets: Hot experts live in the 24GB of VRAM.
Cold experts live in RAM, then SSD.
A lookup table decides where to fetch each one from.

slides.text:
Two more tricks buy extra speed, at a small cost.

Both trade a bit of accuracy for a lot more throughput.
bullets: Quantization shrinks each expert to 2 or 3-bit.
A draft model guesses several tokens at once.
The big model only checks the draft.

slides.text:
**Speed and quality are not the same win here.**

One developer's vision test tripled the error rate against llama.cpp.

Another found the lowest quantization setting hurt real coding accuracy.
The short version, if you want to try this yourself.
bullets: Only a few experts fire per token.
Hot experts on GPU, cold in RAM or disk.
Low-bit quantization buys speed, costs accuracy.
Test quality on your own task first.
